run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Hotel-reservation is failing on the read path frontend -> search -> rate. All 19 pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts and all deployments 1/1 available, and the only failure events in the namespace are the normal 04:40 creation/scaling events, so this is not a crash, OOM, eviction or scheduling problem. The 'rate' Deployment (pod rate-c4d7bcb48-7zkl4) runs a queue-based limiter configured with RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256. Its own metrics show it pinned at that ceiling (completions 317->1504, i.e. ~20/s) while the queue is at capacity (rate_queue_depth 254 of 256) and requests are being dropped (rate_requests_rejected_total 0->855, rate_requests_expired_total 1->1149); admitted /rate.Rate/GetRates server spans spend ~12.7 s before even reaching memcached-rate, while its memcached backend answers in 0.35-0.67 ms and the pod uses only ~0.02 CPU. 'search' (pod search-7769dfc66b-cnx75) calls rate with a 750 ms deadline and up to 3 attempts, so every search request now emits one fast ResourceExhausted plus two ~750 ms DeadlineExceeded rate calls and then fails its own /search.Search/Nearby span; per-request retries inflate rate's offered load to ~2-3x (search_rate_attempts_total 55->1831 vs search_requests_total 54->852 over the same minute). 'frontend' (pod frontend-68745cb99c-d2mzs) returns HTTP 500 on GET /hotels for these failed searches. geo, profile, reservation and rate's memcached backend show no error signals in the sampled traces/logs. The deepest confirmed fault is the rate limiter's saturated/over-capacity queue; search's short deadline plus retries is a second, evidence-backed candidate that aggravates and possibly bootstraps the collapse, and without change history I cannot tell which configuration value deviates from its intended default, so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: All 19 pods in namespace hotel-reservation are phase Running with every container Ready and restartCount 0, and all 19 Deployments report ready=1/available=1; examples: rate-c4d7bcb48-7zkl4, search-7769dfc66b-cnx75, frontend-68745cb99c-d2mzs.
Deployment 'rate' carries the only rate-limiter tunables in the namespace: RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 (plus JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1); no args/command override them.
Deployment 'search' calls the rate service with RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS=50, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER=2.0, RATE_RPC_JITTER=0.2.

Rate-service counters between the 04:41:12 and 04:42:12 scrapes: rate_requests_received_total 317->2613, rate_requests_completed_total 317->1504 (~20/s, its configured ceiling), rate_requests_rejected_total 0->855, rate_requests_expired_total 1->1149, rate_queue_depth 254 against rate_queue_capacity 256, rate_backend_qps_limit 20, rate_in_flight 0.

Admitted rate server spans show ~12.7-12.8 s of pre-work queueing: e.g. rate /rate.Rate/GetRates span 3f5d00e0d9b1c3b4 starts at 1795495289647603 (04:41:29.647) with duration 12,710,210 us and its memcached_get_multi_rate child 2f8a8f4cee4f67e0 only starts at 1795495302357059 (04:41:42.357); the same ~12.73-12.80 s pattern repeats in traces at 04:42:09-04:42:11.

Rate rejects work immediately when the queue is full: rate /rate.Rate/GetRates server spans with error=true and otel.status_code=ERROR return in 15-26 us (e.g. span 1246ebdcb44c5255 26 us, span 06e2a2a47843f98d 20 us, span 042.../043d820bdc00de02 19 us), matching the ResourceExhausted gRPC code search logs.

Search pod search-7769dfc66b-cnx75 logged 790 error-pattern lines in the 10 minutes to 04:42:12 (frontend 6, every other hotel pod 0-6), all of the form 'services/search/server.go:252 > downstream request failed dependency=rate grpc_code=DeadlineExceeded' with interspersed 'grpc_code=ResourceExhausted' between 04:42:04 and 04:42:11.

Each failing search request emits three rate attempts: two search-side /rate.Rate/GetRates client spans of ~750 ms with error=true (750,022-751,006 us, the 750 ms RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS) and one sub-millisecond error span (539-839 us), inside a failing search /search.Search/Nearby server span.

Frontend user impact is observed on its own spans: frontend HTTP GET /hotels spans carry error=true with http.status_code=500 and durations 880,716-2,410,862 us, each the parent of a failing /search.Search/Nearby span (e.g. trace 67c4fee0f811cd81, 7c6e1b7ad0343937, 25466d3e482ca7ab).

Search's retries multiply load on rate: over the same 04:41:12-04:42:12 interval search_rate_attempts_total rose 55->1831 while search_requests_total rose 54->852, i.e. ~2.1 rate attempts per search request, and rate_requests_received_total rose 317->2613 (~38/s) against a 20/s limiter ceiling.

rate-c4d7bcb48-7zkl4 is not CPU-bound: container_cpu_usage_seconds_total rate is 0.020-0.028 cores against a 1-core CPU limit, and the query for container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total over hotel-reservation returned nothing (unchecked, not zero).

rate's own downstreams are healthy in the same traces: memcached_get_multi_rate spans (child of the queued GetRates spans) last 355-665 us with no error status, and geo /geo.Geo/Nearby spans last 32-70 us with no error status.

profile-7f5f54c8-prglq, reservation-7d77c6cb59-ksdfb and the geo pod produced no error lines in 04:40:00-04:42:12; the only matches for the broad error pattern were their benign startup lines 'Tune: GetMemCTimeout 2' at 04:40:18/04:40:23.

No pod-damage events exist: events across all namespaces grouped by involvedObject.kind/namespace/reason show for hotel-reservation only Deployment ScalingReplicaSet (19), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate (19) and Pod Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started (19 each) around 04:40, with no Evicted/OOMKilled/FailedScheduling/Unhealthy/Failed entries for that namespace.

The alerting rules, read after the authorized window ended, showed HighRequestErrorRate firing for search (value 0.8, activeAt 2026-11-24T04:42:26Z) and frontend (value 1.0, activeAt 04:43:26Z), HighRequestLatency firing for rate (P95 10000 ms, activeAt 04:42:26Z) and HighRequestRate pending for rate (50.3 req/s, activeAt 04:44:26Z); these describe the state when the rules were read, not the incident-time state.

Second candidate cause: search's client policy (RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750 with RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3) converts the limiter's multi-second queue wait into DeadlineExceeded and then re-injects each request 2-3 times, so a transient burst self-sustains an offered load above rate's 20 req/s ceiling; search-side counters (1831 attempts vs 852 requests) and the per-request two ~750 ms timeouts plus one fast rejection support this, but I could not establish whether this policy or the limiter's capacity is the deviating setting.

Rejected: rate's slowness comes from its data backend. memcached_get_multi_rate spans inside the queued GetRates spans take 355-665 us and mongo_rate is only reached on cache misses (2-7 spans), so neither memcached-rate nor mongodb-rate explains the 12.7 s waits.

Rejected: pod crash, OOM, eviction or resource shortage. All pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, deployments are 1/1 available, CPU limits are 1 core with usage ~0.02 cores on rate, and no Evicted/OOMKilled/FailedScheduling events exist for hotel-reservation in the window.

Advisory: treat the rate limiter as the capacity bottleneck - either raise RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT / add rate replicas so the offered ~25-38 req/s fits, or shed load earlier with bounded queue wait; and separately align search's RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS with the limiter's queue latency and cap/disable retries on ResourceExhausted to stop the retry amplification.

gaps: Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so I could not determine whether RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 / RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 on Deployment rate, or RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750 / RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 on Deployment search, is the value that deviates from the intended configuration, or when and by which object it was set.

Only two samples of the rate limiter counters exist inside the window (04:41:12 and 04:42:12) because the application was created at ~04:40:12-04:40:24; the state before 04:41:12 and the exact moment the queue became saturated are unknown, and rate_queue_depth read 254 at both scrapes while received==completed==317 at the first scrape, so that gauge's meaning is not fully determined.

Trace views are biased samples (Jaeger keeps recent traces only; traces_search returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE and the by-tag views reported 'more may exist'), so no failure rate or complete call graph was derived; the per-service error counter traces_span_metrics_calls_total showed only one search /rate.Rate/GetRates error series at 04:42:12 while sampled traces already contained frontend 500s, so its error coverage is incomplete.
The load source is not a pod in namespace hotel-reservation (no load-generator pod/deployment is present), so the generator's target rate and whether it changed during the window are unknown.

I did not inspect Kafka or Redis (not part of this application's observed call path, which uses memcached-rate/mongodb-rate/mongodb-profile and consul), so those integrations remain unchecked rather than healthy; other namespaces/apps (e.g. astronomy-shop, openebs, observe) were only seen via events and were not investigated.

Whether the queue saturation or search's retry amplification started first cannot be ordered from the available two-point metric data, so the single originating object between rate's limiter settings and search's retry/deadline policy remains unproven.
next_steps: Compare the live env of Deployments rate and search against the deployment baseline/manifest (or GitOps history) to see which value was changed before 04:40:12.

If change history becomes available, check whether rate's pod template or env changed during the window; a template change would identify the faulting object, otherwise treat the limiter capacity and search retry policy as tuning candidates.

Watch rate_queue_depth, rate_requests_rejected_total, rate_requests_expired_total and search_rate_timeouts_total once RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT or the search timeout is adjusted, to confirm the chain rate -> search -> frontend before closing the incident.
